competency_fulfillment.rationale: The packet successfully fulfills both aspects of the competency by asking students to recognize line types (e.g., 'Two lines that never meet, no matter how far they extend, are called ___.') and assessing the 'draw' component through procedural knowledge (e.g., 'To draw parallel lines using a ruler and a set square, what is the correct technique?').

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: All three required line types are well-represented. Students are tested on parallel lines ('Look at the model: two straight lines that run side by side and never meet ( || ). What type of lines are they?'), intersecting lines ('Look at the letter 'X'. The two crossing line segments form ___.'), and perpendicular lines ('Look at the letter 'T'. The vertical and horizontal segments meet to form ___.').

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The language and conceptual load are perfectly suited for Grade 3 learners. Using familiar contextual models like letters ('Look at the letter 'X'. The two crossing line segments form ___.') and simple definitions ('Two lines that cross at exactly one point are called ___.') appropriately anchors the geometric concepts.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The samples demonstrate a strong variety of problem structures, including standard definitions ('Two lines that meet at a right angle (90°) are called ___.'), visual/symbolic recognition, conceptual relationships ('Are all perpendicular lines also intersecting lines?'), and drawing mechanics ('To draw perpendicular lines forming a square right angle, which tools can you use together?').

competency_alignment.rationale: Every item is strictly aligned with the MATATAG competency text. The questions do not exceed Grade 3 boundaries (e.g., by introducing transversals or complex angle measurements), focusing purely on recognizing and drawing the three explicit line types ('Are all perpendicular lines also intersecting lines?').

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The assessment format is highly scalable for a digital environment. Using tool selection and procedural steps ('To draw perpendicular lines forming a square right angle, which tools can you use together?') is an effective workaround for assessing drawing skills within a multiple-choice structure.
